§1 — What transfers from JT-60SA

The JT-60SA work establishes a method: a converter built from its topology, a few physical parameters identified from facility data, design components inserted without fitting, and a pre-registered prediction. ITER's coil supplies are larger but of the same families, so the library carries over: thyristor converters, switching networks for breakdown, fast discharge units, and reactive-power compensation and harmonic filtering on the AC side. ITER also uses IGBT converters, which the library does not yet model. The JT-60SA work answers whether a good model can be identified from a lot of facility data; this plan carries that answer to ITER.

ITER's data is its converters' tests on dummy loads, archived in CODAC UDA. Those tests are the dataset the ITER model is identified from, and the identified PF converter model (§6) is this plan's main deliverable. Finding the tests (§4), measuring their ripple (§5) and fitting the converters (§6) do not wait on JT-60SA. The JT-60SA verdict in filter-grounding-prediction decides how far the library's prediction of a whole coil circuit can be trusted, so it gates §3 only. §3 does not wait for §6: the measured test waveforms are not in UDA and ITER has no coil data yet, so §3 predicts the PF circuit from design values and the machine description, and §6 narrows its converter inputs when test data arrives.

§2 — The ITER coil-supply topology, from documents

ITER's coil circuit is more complex than JT-60SA's. The machine description's Stage 1 and Stage 2 supply set (pf_active, pulse 111001 run 204) has 14 supplies. The VS1 vertical-stabilisation supply is one supply of six series units, VS1-1 to VS1-6, connected between the two common nodes of the PF2 to PF5 branches, so it carries their imbalance current, PF2 + PF3 − PF4 − PF5; an earlier description of one VS1 unit per coil with a lifting pair is superseded by that record. The supplies are a mix of thyristor and IGBT converters. The PF supplies come first; the CS and TF supplies are out of scope until the PF model stands.

Document the topology of one PF circuit and of the VS1 loop end to end, with citations:

  • converter units, each one's type (thyristor or IGBT), pulse number or switching frequency, transformer phase groups and ratings;
  • the AC supply (400 kV grid, reactive-power compensation and harmonic filters);
  • the switching network and fast discharge units;
  • the grounding scheme and coil insulation limits.

Check what the IMAS Data Dictionary's pf_active supply structure can hold, so the model's parameters have a home.

Leads to start from, each to be confirmed or ruled out with a citation. The ITER machine definitions in the DINA sources (~/Code/dina/machines/ and ~/Code/DINA-IMAS/machines/), which carry the PF and CS circuits a scenario code drives, including converter voltage limits and switching-network resistors where present. The ITER machine description held as IMAS data, whose pf_active circuit and supply arrays, if filled, are a circuit definition in the Data Dictionary's own terms. The coil-circuit work in ~/Code/nova. The documents and facility records in the imas-codex graph. The ITER Document Management system and the published descriptions of the coil power supply system (AC/DC converters, switching networks, fast discharge units, reactive-power compensation and harmonic filtering). The magnet cold-test bench circuit, a test-facility converter feeding a TF coil with a fast discharge unit, documented in ~/Code/mctb/docs/research/mctb-discharge-fit.html §1 and ~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/discharge-fit/fdu-circuit.svg. The cited table and the drawn circuit are written up in docs/research/iter-coil-supply-topology.html.

Done when a cited topology table and a drawn circuit, in docs/figures/iter-power-supply-model/, exist for one PF circuit and for the VS1 loop, with every converter unit's type stated. The mapping of their parameters to pf_active fields is recorded, including the parameters the Data Dictionary has no field for. Every search that returns nothing also records a fact known to be present that the same route did find, so an empty result is a measurement rather than a broken route.

§3 — One ITER PF circuit, predicted

A thin caller, scripts/iter/pf_circuit.py, reads the §2 topology table and its design values, takes a unit's identified parameters from §6 in their place where §6 has fitted that unit, and assembles them into SupplyModel in src/power_convertor/supply.py. SupplyModel already owns the composition of the switching-function bridges (BridgePair in src/power_convertor/bridge.py) with the loop network (BoosterLoop and GroundingSystem in src/power_convertor/filter_network.py) and the ripple-spectrum prediction, so it is extended rather than re-implemented: several series sources for the VS1 loop, the ITER grounding, an IGBT source where §2 finds one, and a sampling rate that is a parameter rather than JT-60SA's. A unit §6 has not fitted takes its §2 design values, marked as such. Three converter inputs the documents do not yet give are carried as stated ranges rather than single values: the commutation reactance (from the converter transformer's short-circuit impedance and the 66 kV network level), the phase displacement between the series units of one string, and how the series units share the voltage. The coil self and mutual inductances, the circuit inductances and the passive structure come from §7, which takes them from ITER's machine description through nova by the route the JT-60SA coil-circuit work established (jt60sa-coil-circuit-model). The caller predicts the coil-voltage ripple spectrum and the coil terminal voltages to ground across the circuit's operating range. Every converter unit in the loop is a ripple source and is instantiated: at JT-60SA the base supplies, not only the boosters, set the ripple left after the filters were fitted (jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §9).

The prediction is judged by the two things ripple threatens in the coils, not by the spectrum alone. For Paschen breakdown the measure is the peak instantaneous voltage to ground, and between adjacent conductors, wherever insulation faces helium at degraded vacuum: the in-cryostat coil terminals, feeders, joints and instrumentation leads. That peak is the DC share each terminal carries under the symmetrical grounding, plus the common-mode ripple, which moves both terminals together and to which each series unit contributes according to its place in the string, plus the commutation notches and switching transients. It is compared with the helium Paschen curve the magnet cold-test work already computes (~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/cryostat-vacuum/paschen_margin.py). For quench detection the measure is the residual differential ripple in each detection section: the inductive ripple voltage the compensation leaves through section imbalance, plus common-mode ripple converted by finite common-mode rejection, within the detection electronics' bandwidth and after any aliasing by their sampling, compared with the detection threshold over its holding time.

Both measures need the circuit beyond the converters: the stray capacitances of the windings, feeders and transformer secondaries to ground, the grounding resistors, the mutual coupling of PF2 to PF5 through the VS1 string, and the detection section layout, compensation scheme and electronics bandwidth. Each is cited from documents or marked as an assumed value. Before a coil is treated as lumped, its first winding resonance is checked to lie above the ripple band; where it does not, the winding is divided into sections so that the voltage distribution along it is carried.

The prediction is blind and is frozen before any fast dummy-load or coil data is read: the lead decided on 14 October 2026 that it runs with the JT-60SA verdict recorded rather than waiting for the booster-model repair. Its inputs come from §2, §7 and the commutation design (iter-commutation-design), and it carries a declared error band built from two parts: the input ranges, each propagated by evaluating the model at both ends (the commutation reactance, the AC-busbar reference side, the firing angle swept through 90°, the firing of the series units under the sequential law, the passive screening), and the model error the JT-60SA verdict measured, about 2.3 dB on the characteristic lines at steady current and 10 to 13 dB on the non-characteristic lines and during current swings. The IGBT units of VS1 are ripple sources too: their carrier lines and sidebands (1600 Hz rectifier, 500 Hz inverter, 45° interleave) and their switching edges enter the same circuit. Where an input the margins need is not given (the grounding resistors, the stray capacitances, the quench-detection layout, compensation, bandwidth and threshold), the Paschen and quench-detection margins are reported as functions of that input over a stated range rather than as single values.

Done when the prediction is recorded in docs/research/iter-pf-circuit-prediction.html, with its figures in docs/figures/iter-pf-circuit-prediction/ and every input traced to a §2 citation, the machine description, a §6 fit, or a stated range marked as assumed, and two controls hold. The positive control: the same caller, given every input filter-grounding-prediction §4 scored for EF5 (the 2021-fitted parameters, the 2023 structure, the design filter, the grounding and the 2023 operating point, booster and base supply both), and passing its clean spectrum through the same measurement chain that section's scoring entry point applies (the library measurement in src/power_convertor/measurement.py), reproduces that section's recorded predicted EF5 line amplitudes from 6f to 30f to 0.01 dB, and the phases that section's scoring entry point fits from the same model output to 0.1°, so the ITER caller adds no error of its own. How far that prediction is from the measured EF5 lines is the JT-60SA verdict gate g-ipsm-1 carries, not this control's measure. The negative controls change one input at a time, and each has its own spectral expectation. Changing the supply frequency from 50 Hz to 61.1 Hz must move every predicted line's frequency by the same ratio, 61.1/50, while its amplitude moves by less than the stated tolerance (§6 measured the amplitude change to be well under it). Changing a twelve-pulse pair to an in-phase six-pulse pair must bring up the 6f and 18f lines that the twelve-pulse phase shift cancels, while the 12f and 24f lines stay at their frequencies, as BridgePair.harmonic_phasors computes them. A library that kept either JT-60SA value internally fails one of these checks, which is the specialisation this section exists to rule out. The record states, for each in-cryostat location named, the predicted peak voltage to ground and its margin to the helium Paschen minimum, and for each quench-detection section the in-band residual differential ripple and its margin to the detection threshold, each with its inputs cited or marked as assumed, and, for each input carried as a range, both margins at each end of that range.

§4 — The dummy-load tests, found in UDA

Find ITER's power-converter tests on dummy loads in CODAC UDA, PF supplies first. For each test, record the converter unit and its type, the date, the load (resistance and inductance), the operating points (current, voltage, firing angle or duty cycle), the channels with their sampling rates, and the pulse or time window. Sampling rate matters because the JT-60SA work showed a 4 kHz channel aliasing the converter harmonics above 2 kHz, so a test whose fastest channel cannot resolve the characteristic lines is recorded as such. Factory acceptance tests held outside UDA and the first coil energisation are listed as later data, with where and when they are expected.

The access route is CODAC UDA, and the mctb repository already reads it: the recipe and its traps are in ~/Code/mctb/docs/research/mctb-uda-access.html, and the client in ~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/uda_servers.py (slow archive on io-ls-udasrv2, fast SDN channels and discharge records on 4509dr-srv-5002, port 3090, after ml MINT). io-ls-udasrv1 is reserved for control-room operators and is never read. The channels the mctb scripts under ~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/uda-access/ and ~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/discharge-fit/ read are the known-present control for this route; the cold-test bench's own converter is a secondary dataset. Search UDA for the coil power supply plant systems (PF converters first, then the VS1 converters, switching networks, fast discharge units and reactive-power compensation), for the variables and time windows of their dummy-load tests, and for any circuit definition UDA serves. The UDA client sources in ~/Code/codac/ and the SDN interface in ~/Code/dina/imas/interface/dina_sdn.f90 name signals worth checking. The table is written up in docs/research/iter-dummy-load-tests.html, and the traces of the tests found are saved under data/iter/, which is gitignored like the JT-60SA traces.

The searches share one UDA reader, src/power_convertor/uda.py, rather than a copy of the read code per script. A robust UDA reader is needed beyond this plan, so it is built from what already exists: the server rules and per-study readers in the mctb repository (~/Code/mctb/docs/figures/uda_servers.py and its data modules), the read traps measured in ~/Code/mctb/docs/research/mctb-uda-access.html §6, and the query layer in ~/Code/nova/nova/datachain/uda.py. It carries no project imports or channel names, so it can later move to a shared package.

Done when the table names each dummy-load test found, PF supplies first, with its converter unit and type, date, load, operating points, channels, sampling rates and access route, and the traces of at least one PF converter test are saved under data/iter/. If UDA holds no dummy-load test, the table records each search made beside a known-present mctb channel read by the same route in the same session, so an empty result is a measurement rather than a broken route, and names where else the tests may be held.

§5 — Ripple in the dummy-load tests

Process the §4 traces and decide whether ripple can be assessed from the dummy-load tests at all. For each tested PF converter and operating point, measure the line amplitudes at the converter's characteristic frequencies: multiples of 12f for a twelve-pulse thyristor unit, and the switching frequency with its sidebands for an IGBT unit. The caller is scripts/iter/dummy_load_ripple.py: it loads the §4 windows from data/iter/ with each channel's sampling rate and acquisition settings, and passes them to the measures in src/power_convertor/signals.py, the folding in src/power_convertor/fold.py and, where the ITER acquisition chain is known, the acquisition model in src/power_convertor/measurement.py, rather than writing parallel ones or relying on their JT-60SA defaults. Three things decide whether the tests can carry a model: the sampling rate against the characteristic lines, the noise floor against the line amplitudes, and the spread of a line across repeated operating points.

The test data also describes its own load and operating point, so neither is taken on trust. The load resistance and inductance are fitted from the load voltage and current as v = R i + L di/dt, ramps giving L and flat tops R. identify in src/power_convertor/circuit.py fits the ten-coil JT-60SA swing loop and cannot take a single load, so a single-load fit is added beside it that reuses its robust least squares (_huber) and its filtered derivative (_derivative). Where voltage is measured at the converter terminals the fitted load includes the busbars, which is the circuit the converter saw. The firing angle is read from the per-unit ALPHA channels and checked against the angle that inverts the DC regulation, Vdc = Vd0 cos α − (3Xc/π) I per six-pulse bridge; the same regression of DC voltage on firing angle and current gives the commutation reactance Xc even where the sampling rate cannot resolve the ripple. Three further checks decide what the tests can say about the coils: whether conduction was continuous, whether the tested firing angles and currents overlap coil operation (a superconducting coil at flat top holds full current at almost zero DC voltage, near α = 90°, where the twelve-pulse ripple is largest), and whether each test drove one converter unit or a series string.

Done when docs/research/iter-dummy-load-tests.html carries, for each tested PF converter unit, a figure in docs/figures/iter-dummy-load-tests/ of measured line amplitude against operating point, with every line marked resolved or aliased by its channel's sampling rate, a table per tested unit of the fitted load R and L, the firing-angle and current ranges, continuous conduction, the commutation reactance from DC regulation, and the overlap with coil operation, and a stated verdict on whether the tests can identify the converter. The negative control is a source-off window: the converter blocked with the measurement chain live, which is not the same as deblocked at zero reference, a state that still produces ripple at JT-60SA (measurement.measure over its default IDLE span, before the plasma pulse). The source-off window must show no characteristic line above the noise floor before a line is counted as converter ripple. Where no source-off window exists, an off-frequency estimate sets the noise floor only, and each line's source is recorded as unresolved between converter output and pickup, for §6 to weigh before fitting it.

§6 — The ITER PF converter model, identified from the dummy-load tests

Apply the JT-60SA method to the dummy-load tests. Each tested PF converter is built from its §2 topology, and its few physical parameters are identified from part of its tests: for a thyristor bridge, the line voltage and commutation reactance, which fit_base_supply in src/power_convertor/supply.py already identifies from the twelve- and twenty-four-pulse lines; for an IGBT unit, the parameters of a switching model the library does not yet hold, added beside SixPulseBridge in src/power_convertor/bridge.py rather than in a parallel module. A dummy load is a known resistance and inductance, so the converter is identified without the coil and the coupled circuit; §3 then puts the identified converter into the coil circuit.

The caller is scripts/iter/identify_pf_converter.py. It loads the §4 windows, builds each converter from its §2 topology with the ITER acquisition settings (sampling rate, bandwidth and timing skew) passed explicitly, because fit_base_supply otherwise builds a twelve-pulse SupplyModel with JT-60SA defaults such as its 104.57 µs skew and its 32 kHz input_rate, and runs the split fixed before the fit. fit_base_supply exposes bandwidth and skew, but not the sampling rate or the phase shift between the bridges, and it scores only the 12f and 24f lines. §6 extends its signature with the input rate, the phase shift and the scored orders, and passes them to the SupplyModel it builds; each keeps its current default, so the JT-60SA callers are unchanged, and it is sequenced with any open run that holds src/power_convertor/supply.py. The split, the tolerance and the converter identities are committed in docs/research/iter-pf-converter-fit.html before the fit runs; the identified parameters, with their units, converter identity and the traces they came from, are written to docs/figures/iter-pf-converter-fit/parameters.json, which §3 reads.

§6 starts only when §2 has documented the tested converter's topology and §5's verdict is that the tests can identify it. If §4 finds no dummy-load test, or §5 finds that the tests cannot carry a model, §6 is deferred: §3 takes §2 design values for every unit, and the plan records which data would unblock the fit, such as factory acceptance records held outside UDA or the first coil energisation.

Done when the fit and held-out tests are named in the committed docs/research/iter-pf-converter-fit.html before the fit, the identified parameters in docs/figures/iter-pf-converter-fit/parameters.json predict the held-out tests' characteristic lines within the tolerance recorded there before the fit (as filter-grounding-prediction records its 3 dB), the held-out verdict is recorded in the same document, and the negative control misses the same held-out lines by more than that tolerance: the converter built as an in-phase six-pulse pair (phase shift 0 rather than 30°), which predicts 6f and 18f lines far above the residual a working twelve-pulse unit leaves, scored on those lines against the measured residual while the fit itself is scored on 12f and 24f. The fit also records how sharply the held-out lines bound the commutation reactance: the range of Xc whose predicted 12f and 24f lines stay within the tolerance at the held-out operating points. A doubled reactance moves those lines by less than 3 dB at many operating points, so where the range spans more than a factor of two the verdict states that those operating points do not identify Xc, rather than reporting a fitted value. A change of supply frequency is not used as a control, because it moves the line amplitudes by well under the tolerance.

§7 — ITER coil and passive-structure coupling, from the machine description

§3 needs the coils' self and mutual inductances and the passive structure's coupling to them. They come from ITER's machine description through nova, by the route the JT-60SA coil-circuit work validated: nova's conductor set, built from OP2's pf_active and pf_passive at nominal resistivity, predicted 8 of 9 measured EF-pair transfer functions within 4 to 8 % rms of M/L over 0.1 to 30 Hz with no fit (jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §5). The export there, scripts/jt60sa/nova_passive_matrices.py, is written for OP2. Its body is lifted into one function that takes the active and passive machine-description entries and their group labels; the JT-60SA script becomes a caller of it and scripts/iter/nova_passive_matrices.py is the second. The output loads through PassiveStructure in src/power_convertor/passive_structure.py, which already reduces a filament set to decay modes and the coupled terminal ratio.

The sources are in /work/imas/shared/imasdb/ITER_MACHINE_DESCRIPTION/3/: pf_active pulse 111001 run 204 (the Stage 1 and Stage 2 supply set; 14 coils, CS3U to CS3L, PF1 to PF6 and the VS3 in-vessel coils; run 104 is the Stage 1 supply set) and pf_passive pulse 115004 run 6 (vacuum vessel, thermal shield and divertor, 210 loops) with pulse 124001 run 3 (cryostat and its thermal shield, 248 loops). The reduced descriptions 115005/3 and 124002/3 and the blanket panels 116001/3 are compared as variants rather than summed. Each loop's resistance or resistivity is taken from the description where it is given, and from the material's nominal resistivity, cited, where it is not.

The coupling is then reduced to what the converters see. The pf_active circuit connections define the circuits: the VS1 circuit places the PF2 to PF5 branches between two common nodes with the VS1 supply across them, so VS1 drives the imbalance PF2 + PF3 − PF4 − PF5. The section reports the circuit inductance matrix of the PF and VS1 circuits; the inductance each supply sees with the other supplies open and with them shorted; the passive decay modes with their time constants; and each PF circuit's terminal impedance with the passive structure from 0.1 Hz to 5 kHz, which spans the twelve-pulse lines at 600 Hz and above. One filament across a shell's thickness holds while the skin depth exceeds that thickness, so the frequency at which it stops holding is computed for each passive group and marked on the impedance figure, and the ripple-band values carry their own validity limit.

Done when the lifted export reproduces the merged JT-60SA matrices (data/jt60sa/passive_structure/matrices.json) to floating-point tolerance through the JT-60SA caller; the ITER matrices are written to /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/iter/passive_structure/ and PassiveStructure loads them; the coil inductance matrix is symmetric and positive definite, and each coil's self-inductance is compared with a published ITER value where one is found, cited, or marked as having none; two controls hold, removing the passive structure leaves the DC inductances unchanged while changing the terminal impedance above the first decay mode's corner frequency, and reversing one coil's turns flips the sign of that coil's mutuals and of no other; and the results are recorded in docs/research/iter-coil-coupling.html with figures in docs/figures/iter-coil-coupling/ (the coil and circuit inductance matrices, the decay modes, and the terminal impedances with their validity limits). The nova runs are heavy and run on the fleet allocation or an all_debug partition, with their logs kept.

§8 — When the scenarios load the supplies most

§3 sweeps the firing angle and current over their ranges. ITER's own scenario simulations say where the supplies actually operate: the DINA scenarios in the IMAS scenario database hold the driven-coil solution, coil currents and coil voltages for all 14 coils at 5 ms (the 15 MA H-mode case, pulse 105001 run 6, covers 0 to 391 s, and its coil voltages reach the supply limits: PF2 to PF4 3.15 kV, PF1, PF6 and CS 2.1 kV, CS1 4.2 kV). The coils therefore need not be re-simulated: DINA has solved them self-consistently with the plasma. This section maps those coil series to each supply and series unit through the machine-description circuits (VS1 carries PF2 + PF3 − PF4 − PF5), turns each unit's voltage and current into a firing angle with the commutation design, and ranks the intervals that load each supply most: by voltage and the time at its limit, by current, by power, by time near 90° at high current where twelve-pulse ripple is largest, by current zero crossings, and by the coil dI/dt quench detection must compensate. Each ranked interval is named by its scenario phase. A check compares DINA's coil voltages with L·dI/dt from §7's matrix in steady-plasma intervals, without fitting. The scenarios covered are 105001/6 (15 MA), 105003/6 (10 MA), 105006/7 (3 MA), one first-plasma case and one PFPO-1 case.

Done when docs/research/iter-scenario-supply-loading.html and docs/figures/iter-scenario-supply-loading/ give, for each covered scenario, every PF supply's and VS1's voltage, current and firing-angle timeline at both ends of the commutation-reactance range, with the top loading intervals per measure marked and tabulated by scenario phase, and the 12f and 24f converter lines at each ranked interval; the coupling check's residual is reported with its attribution; a synthetic two-branch test gives the expected supply operating points and ranking, and reversing one coil's current changes the VS1 current as the circuit predicts (logged); reckon audit-doc reports zero errors.

The 2024 re-baseline replaced First Plasma with Start of Research Operation; the converter stages keep their earlier scopes (ITER, BSBF 2022, slide 4: Stage 1 is the domestic agencies' First Plasma supply, Stage 2 the ITER-procured Post First Plasma supply), and ITER's 1 September 2025 article states that the 12 Stage 2 units are needed before the machine can turn on, so SRO needs both stages.

§2 landed: the cited topology table and drawn circuits exist for the PF2 branch and the VS1 loop, every converter unit's type is stated (corrected from the design documents at 9a9745a), the VS1 arrangement is settled from the machine description and the pf_active mapping is recorded (merge 1ab0dc3, review 108). Two follow-ons stay open: the drawing test counts labels and would not catch a disconnected branch, and the receipt does not capture every field the mapping table cites. The DC interconnecting busbar design (FN7MW9) is being extracted and will extend the register. evidence

IDM FN7MW9 v1.0, the Stage 2 DC interconnecting busbar design, is extracted (merge 8e75f37, review 103): busbar resistance 2.5 µΩ/m (PF/CS) and 3.6 µΩ/m (VS), aluminium conductors 120 × 200 mm and 80 × 200 mm per pole, 13.2 kV AC insulation with 48 kV DC and 58 kV impulse withstand; it confirms the six-unit VS1 series string and the PF1 and PF6 Stage 1 + Stage 2 strings at 55 kA, prints no busbar inductance or capacitance, and carries nothing on the AC-side commutation. fragment

Lead for the coil coupling in this section, from the JT-60SA coil-circuit work (not yet merged, under review): nova's passive structure, built from the OP2 machine description's pf_active and pf_passive (155 filaments: 98 vessel, 57 cryostat) at nominal resistivity, predicts 8 of 9 measured 2021 EF-pair transfer functions within 4 to 8 % rms of M/L over 0.1 to 30 Hz, leave-one-pair-out, with no fit; fitted resistivity scales (1.23 vessel, 0.89 cryostat) barely change it, and a free identified-loop model did much worse (15 to 825 %). The code is scripts/jt60sa/nova_passive_matrices.py (exports coil and filament L, R and mutual matrices) and src/power_convertor/passive_structure.py (decay modes and the coupled terminal ratio). For ITER this suggests taking the coupling from the machine description's pf_passive through nova rather than fitting it, if ITER's description carries its passive structures. Fold into the section's text when the code lands and that check is made.

The lead confirms that ITER's machine description includes its passive structure, and that no measured ITER coil data exists yet because the machine is not complete. The coupling for this section therefore comes from the machine description through nova, as the JT-60SA result supports, rather than from a fit.

Lead decision (15 October 2026): JT-60SA validates the method, not JT-60SA's converter models. ITER has no booster, so the booster model's error does not belong in ITER's ripple band. Gate g-ipsm-1 is already closed; this decision governs how §3's declared band is rebuilt. It comes from three parts that carry over:

  1. nova's coil-to-coil coupling error at the harmonics: jt60sa-coil-circuit-model §9 scores it against the 52 measured booster-test ratios, with no converter model in the loop, as a per-harmonic amplitude and phase band.
  2. The twelve-pulse thyristor modelling error, from the base-supply work rather than the booster.
  3. ITER's own converter data. The PF1-1 and PF6-1 dummy-load firing angles agree with the mean-voltage law to a median of −3.4° and −3.0° (p10/p90 within about ±9°) over 20–55 kA in rectification. The TF cold tests and the HIOKI recordings, now located, follow.

IDM FFZXDR v1.2 (approved 31 Aug 2026), the turnover scope for PF2–PF6 and Dummy Load 2, holds no test data: it hands the converters' I&C cubicles and cables from construction to commissioning. Its leads to the test data: the System Commissioning Plan of PF Power Converters (8YDU27 v3.1), which governs the commissioning tests and their records; Dummy Load 2 in B33-OUT-WEST, with its P&ID (X7ZE6B v1.0), cabling diagram (27QT5N v3.6), marked scope (ETNZXK) and the PF2–PF5 and VS1 one-line diagram (3SPASA); the PF2–PF6 one-line diagrams (PK3YQG, PK4TXG, PK6ZEZ, PJZR6N, PK32WW); and the interfaces and services appendix (DJRSMJ). PF1 and its dummy load are not in this package, so the September PF1 tests fall under a separate turnover package. Its PF6 one-line excerpt shows the Stage 1 unit's two 41 MVA transformers as extended delta 0/+15° and 0/−15°, where the Stage 2 design (FMSLSQ v1.1) uses Dd0/Yd11.

The dummy-load controller's archive variables now have documented meanings. IDM 5KT5BJ v1.2, the 2021 test report of the Dummy Load 2 control cubicle, defines MAG-PFCS-DLL2:DL1101-IT as the grounding current, with a 600 mA fault threshold. So the DLL1 DL1101-IT readings of 0–113 on 28 Sep and 7–12 Oct 2026 are ground current, not the dummy-load current that iter-dummy-load-tests.html reads them as. The same report gives the B33 converter-selector codes (CLCNCVTNUM: 12 PF2, 13 PF3, 14 PF4, 15 PF5, 16 VS1, 17–19 CCL1–3, 20–22 CCS1–3, 23–25 PF2/3/4 with VS1), and DLMODE is the dummy-load mode flag. The cabling diagram 27QT5N v3.6 records that the B32 dummy load (DL1) is cabled to PF1-1 and PF6-1. Together with the DLL1 mode (on from 28 Sep) and selector (1 to 2 on 5 Oct) already in the archive, these date each dummy-load session and name its converter. They do not supply the load's voltage or current waveform, which no archived variable has been found to carry. Node uda-dummy-load-sessions derives the session table; a dedicated evidence document will record the signals, sessions, code tables, read recipes and the remaining gap.

The commissioning plan (8YDU27 v3.1) says where the dummy-load waveforms go. A transient-recorder event or manual trigger records the converter's signals in its local buffer. The CCR aggregates them into a DAN stream and publishes it "to DAN archiver server via DAN" (TP-41P1CU-10108, -10506). The Stage 2 I&C slides (FQHFN3) list the DAN table's fields: four bridge currents, the terminal current, four bridge voltages and the terminal voltage. The same plan defines the tests: a 0.3 Ω resistive light load, and the 6.73 mH inductive dummy load at 55 kA for at most 20 s or 27.5 kA for at most 60 s, at least 15 min apart. The PF1 SAT follows Q3JXB, "SAT for PF Converter System". The waveforms are therefore expected in the DAN archive, not in the slow or SDN UDA archives that §4 has searched. Node dan-archive-probe tests whether that archive is readable without io-ls-udasrv1.

The archive does carry the dummy-load tests' currents. On io-ls-udasrv2, MAG-PFCS-PF1/PF6:TCD1101–1106-IT (kA, ~2 s) are the converters' bridge, output and bypass current transducers. PF1 ran on the B32 dummy load from 28 Sep 09:25:59 to 5 Oct 12:37:03 UTC (selector 1). PF6 ran from then on (selector 2). The selector codes are documented in 55S4Q4 Table 9 (B32: 1 PF1 two units, 2 PF6 two units). The output current spans −55 to +55 kA, and the bridges reach 26–29 kA (uda-dummy-load-sessions, merged 09c80a8). No converter voltage variable exists, and 2 s cannot resolve ripple. The fast recordings were searched for and not found: the DAN catalogue on the three permitted hosts holds no PF or plant-system-41 recorder pulse, while an 80 kHz MCTB DAN control reads (dan-archive-probe). The operations server io-ls-udasrv1, read once with the lead's authorisation, mirrors io-ls-udasrv2 and holds none either (dan-operations-probe). The lead reports the IDM site-acceptance folders empty. The dummy load is 6.73 mH ±1 % (6.79 mH computed) and 2.99 mΩ at 25 °C (Q3UJAZ, Q5TGLF). Node iter-pf-dummy-load-evidence writes all of this into one evidence document, with the requests that would close the gap: the PF1-1 and PF6-1 DAN stream names and pulse IDs from the CCR/DAN owner, and the executed test records from the commissioning team.

§ Decisions

Does §3 run now as a blind prediction carrying the JT-60SA error, or wait for the booster-model repair?

The JT-60SA verdict sets how far the library is trusted, and it is in. Running now gives a pre-registered prediction to score against the fast dummy-load data when it arrives; waiting for the booster-model repair would change the error band, not the inputs. The band combines the propagated input ranges with the JT-60SA model error.
